name: 数字雕塑 / Digital Sculpture
summary: Let spatial depth, material, light, camera movement and evolving structures perform the song. Typography is optional rather than the default central sculpture.
principles: Express meaning through physical relationships, material changes and the viewer's movement through space.
Give geometry, light and a clearly staged focal structure enough scale to carry the composition without a headline.
Choose visual density, camera speed and periods of rest for the new song and the user's direction.
typography: Main-scene type is optional: a small engraving, label or spatially placed phrase can be sufficient.
Use dimensional letterforms when they serve this song, rather than requiring a giant title above every scene.
Keep any visible type readable and preserve the quiet lyric-caption layer.
composition: Build visible depth with perspective, occlusion, foreground, middle distance and background relationships.
Vary immersive passages, material close-ups, full sculptural views and open space according to the song.
Keep the main structure large enough to read; preserve a calm bottom caption area.
color: Reflective metal, translucent glass, matte surfaces and selective rim light are possible material relationships, not compulsory assets.
Dark space with cool reflected light and warm accents is one starting point; choose lighting and palette for the new song.
motion: Let structures fold, separate, connect, deform or change material when the lyric meaning supports the action.
Make camera travel, parallax, distance, light and scale reveal those relationships, rather than relying only on rotating a foreground object.
Use quick shifts or sustained movement as the music requires; connect poses and movement directions across scenes.
Calculate object poses, camera and lighting from song time so seeking remains reproducible.
rhythm: Arrange motion around supplied lyric timing and actual available musical evidence; speed and shot duration remain open.
Use supplied beats or measured energy when available, naming them accurately; never present guessed subdivisions or energy rises as verified musical beats.
semantics: Derive the structures, physical interactions and transformations from each new song rather than a fixed storyboard or prop set.
Let light, material and geometry carry the main visible action while bottom captions preserve the actual lyric text.
transitions: Carry a silhouette, structural relationship, material seam, camera trajectory or light direction into the next composition.
Change distance, depth, density and material as the content requires; transitions can be fast and fluid without repeating one effect.
avoid: Defaulting every scene to a giant centered word with geometry behind it.
Replacing each lyric with the same rotating 3D word or the same object-and-ring arrangement.
Endless particle wallpaper, unreadable perspective, a tiny focal sculpture or uncontrolled glow.
Copying the demonstration's phases, prop choices, camera path or durations into a different song.

limitations: Authored creative direction. Example observation and review are recorded separately.
